E013 (LS 0.3->0.2): +0.04 pp, -0.2% time: noise, which refutes 'LS 0.3 beats 0.2 by 0.3 pp'.

Measured prices: compile+fused SGD -14% time (E004); recompile leak about +3 s (E003). Lookahead/EMA about +1 pp at ~0 time (E005), the biggest free gain so far (I under-forecast it). Muon +0.66 pp for +4% (E006). Resizing 24/28/32 -22% time for -0.59 pp (E007, ~3.5 s/pp, a good trade). Aggressive resizing (E011) ~0.9 s/pp, a bad trade: loss turns super-linear once the 32 px tail is <=20% or 20 px is used. Epochs ~2 s/pp (E008). Width 576->512 ~1.6 s/pp (E010). LR decay to 0 on top of EMA: noise (E009). LS 0.2 vs 0.3: noise (E013).

Budget: time ≈ F + V × pixel fraction, F about 0.5-0.8 s, V about 7.5 s at full res. A step is ~26 ms and GPU compute dominates. Host/launch overhead probably 3-6% under the 4-CPU pin. Three compiled regions (fwd/bwd, Muon, fused SGD) plus Python LR writes and a Python Lookahead cap CUDA graphs or break removal at ~0.15-0.35 s. Both risk changing kernels, which moves accuracy ~0.2-0.3 pp at random; with 0.18 pp of margin a systems win can fail on accuracy luck alone.

Accuracy levers: Muon renormalizes filter norms every step, so weight decay only reaches BN biases, whitening bias and head (weak). Muon lr is probably near-optimal. Lookahead's fast-weight reset is probably part of its value; a plain EMA with a ~20-step horizon (alpha ends ~0.77 per 5 steps) is likely worse. Epochs are the reliable way to buy margin (~2 s/pp). Untested cheap levers: a slightly longer 32 px tail with a shorter 24 px head, or BN-stat recompute.

Noise: per-seed std 0.2-0.35 pp, so 3-seed SE ~0.15-0.2 pp. Recipe changes move the mean up to ~0.3 pp. Time noise ~1%.

forecasts.reason: Launch overhead is ~3-6%, so graphs could save 0.1-0.3 s, but Muon and Lookahead stay outside the graph and cudagraph input copies or a leak could eat the gain; likely lands right around the 3% threshold.
Muon renormalizes filter norms, so weight decay only reaches BN biases, whitening bias and head; a weak lever, not +0.3 pp.
GPU is busy most of the time, so the ceiling is ~2-4%; folding augmentation and RNG into the compiled region changes kernels, so bit-identical accuracy is unlikely.
The ramp ends at alpha ~0.77 per 5 steps, so plain EMA only averages the last ~20 steps; losing Lookahead's pull-back regularization should cost ~0.3-0.6 pp.

cruxes: What do held-out seeds 3-12 give on E010? A negative offset means paying back +0.25-0.5 epoch, and every systems win then has to cover that first.
What is the real GPU idle fraction per step under the 4-CPU pin? Over 8% makes CUDA graphs or break removal the next big lever; under 4% means they aren't worth the accuracy-reshuffle risk.
Can a cheap accuracy lever (BN-stat recompute, or moving pixel budget into the 32 px tail) buy ~0.3 pp for under 0.15 s, so that margin can be spent on cutting 0.5 epoch?
